title: Preserve runtime-native Ctrl-C handling on Windows
description:
## Summary

- Deliver Windows Ctrl-C as a real `CTRL_C_EVENT` by writing exact ETX (`0x03`) to each built-in worker's dedicated ConPTY input.
- Add a pass-through control-handler completion observer so managed input wakes only after runtime and package handlers finish.
- Keep the Windows sideband interrupt path cleanup-only: it clears queued, unconsumed input but never sets R or Python interrupt state.
- Advance the strict worker protocol to v7 with payload-free `interrupt_armed` and `interrupt_complete` ordering facts required by public race regressions.

## Motivation

Runtimes and packages can install their own interrupt handlers. In particular, reticulate installs a Windows console handler that coordinates interrupt state between embedded R and Python and returns `TRUE` after consuming the event.

The previous Windows path used `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT` and mcp-repl-specific R/Python interrupt injection. That can bypass or duplicate package policy. It also does not solve managed input cleanly: the runtime main thread is blocked on an mcp-repl input event while Windows runs console handlers on another thread.

The new observer runs before package handlers and returns `FALSE`. It duplicates the Windows-created handler-thread handle and lets a pre-existing watcher wait for that thread to terminate. This supplies an ordering barrier without interpreting the event: R calls `R_CheckUserInterrupt()` and Python calls `PyErr_CheckSignals()` on their normal runtime main threads.

## Public-facing changes

- Ctrl-C reaches Windows runtime and package handlers as event `0` (`CTRL_C_EVENT`), including while a runtime is blocked in managed input.
- A handler that consumes Ctrl-C without scheduling a runtime interrupt leaves the same input operation waiting.
- A handler that schedules runtime state is observed only after the complete handler chain returns.
- Overlapping Ctrl-C calls coalesce onto one native transaction, and later input cannot overtake handler completion or inherit stale interrupt state.
- Built-in R and Python workers and custom workers with ConPTY stdin use native Ctrl-C. Pipe-only Windows custom workers now fail fast with an explicit unsupported-boundary error.
- Startup observer failures preserve their diagnostic, and R shutdown output is retained before the terminal session marker.

## Internal changes

- Add one shared worker-local observer and watcher thread. The handler handles only `CTRL_C_EVENT`, performs a bounded atomic/event handoff, returns `FALSE`, and does not allocate, lock, log, or call runtime APIs.
- Rearm newest-first with add-before-remove alternating callback identities, serialized outside the handler, before readiness and before native delivery.
- Order delivery as cleanup/rearm, `interrupt_armed`, exact ConPTY ETX, handler-thread completion, the runtime checkpoint, `interrupt_complete`, then later readiness.
- Preserve Python runtime-main checkpoint ownership while background managed-stdin consumers remain active, and gate readiness publication against cleanup races.
- Keep accepted input on sideband IPC. Nested Windows sandbox launch byte-for-byte forwards ConPTY input so ETX reaches the inner console.
- Keep CRT stdin read-only; use a separate short-lived read/write `CONIN$` handle only to enable processed input.
- Filter only exact Windows ConPTY lifecycle control sequences, including split reads, and restore unmatched or unarmed bytes.
- Reject direct console attachment/`GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent()` for production because it is more invasive and proves initiation rather than handler completion. There is no Ctrl-Break, runtime-state, polling, fixed-delay, or third-process fallback.

## Relationship to other work

This supersedes the Windows interrupt implementation attempted in #122. It intentionally does not carry forward #122's nullable-prompt, broad `ready`, input-ID, or general discard-ack redesign. Once this replacement lands, #122 should not be merged as-is.

The worker-owned input architecture from #130 and #131 remains intact, and the Python cell/readline distinction from #132 is preserved. This extends the Windows support and test parity established by #1 and #123.

PR #135 remains an open draft and mechanically overlaps architecture/docs, IPC, Python session/FFI, worker supervision, and backend-driver files. There is no semantic dependency; whichever PR lands second will need to rebase.

This change enables package-installed Windows handlers such as reticulate's to remain authoritative and leaves broader sideband redesign work as a separate follow-up.

## Verification

- `cargo test -j 1 --test windows_native_interrupt -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture` — 12/12 passed, including deterministic blocked-handler, sequential-interrupt, coalescing, tail-input, sandbox, background-stdin, publication-race, startup-diagnostic, and R cases.
- With `MCP_REPL_RETICULATE_LIBRARY=C:/tmp/mcp-repl-reticulate-lib` and `MCP_REPL_RETICULATE_PYTHON=C:/Users/kalin/AppData/Local/Python/bin/python.exe`, `cargo test -j 1 --test windows_reticulate_interrupt -- --test-threads=1 --nocapture` — 2/2 passed. R and reticulate Python both returned `42`, with no stale `KeyboardInterrupt`.
- `$env:RUSTFLAGS = "-Dwarnings"; cargo check`
- `$env:RUSTFLAGS = "-Dwarnings"; cargo build`
- `python3 tests/run_integration_tests.py --binary target/debug/mcp-repl` — 21/21 applicable scenarios passed.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `$env:RUSTFLAGS = "-Dwarnings"; cargo test --quiet` — all 478 library tests and every discovered integration binary passed.
- `cargo +nightly fmt`
- `$env:RUSTFLAGS = "-Dwarnings"; cargo build --release --locked`
- `cargo test --test docs_contracts` — 20/20 passed.
- `git diff --check`

title: Release 0.3.0
description:
## Summary

Release 0.3.0 by changing the Cargo package version from `0.3.0-dev` to `0.3.0`. This prepares the repository for the immutable `v0.3.0` tag-driven release workflow after merge.

## User-facing changes

See the release notes below. The release includes PyPI packaging, Python cell execution, reset via Ctrl-D, output/session ordering improvements, sandbox updates, and platform packaging updates.

## Internal changes

- Updates only `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` package version metadata.
- Leaves tag creation and publishing to the documented post-merge release process.

## Release notes

## mcp-repl 0.3.0

### Install and upgrade notes

- Added a PyPI distribution as `posit-mcp-repl`, usable with `pipx`, `uv tool install`, or one-off `uvx posit-mcp-repl`. (#142, #160)
- Removed the separate `repl_reset` tool. Session resets now use `\u0004` (Ctrl-D / EOF) through `repl`, with any remaining input run in the fresh session. (#157)
- Renamed `--sandbox inherit` to `--sandbox inherit-codex`; the old spelling remains a compatibility alias. (#167)
- Release binaries no longer include `--debug-repl`; it remains available in debug/dev builds. (#149)

### REPL behavior

- Python submissions now run as complete cells, not line-oriented interactive input. This gives persistent cell globals, final-expression display through `sys.displayhook`, and stdin routing only when Python is waiting for input. (#132)
- Improved R plotting so console plot sizing options affect the live managed graphics device while plots are drawn, including new `console.plot.asp` support. (#147)
- Improved R startup errors when `R` or `R_HOME` cannot be resolved. (#158)

### Output and session handling

- Reworked output handling so normal replies, pager output, files-mode bundles, images, stderr, server notices, and transcripts share one ordering model. (#138, #148, #152)
- Improved reset behavior so Ctrl-D returns old-session shutdown output before fresh-session output, without leaking abandoned timed-out output into later replies. (#159, #164)
- Cleaned up worker session temp directories when workers are dropped. (#137)

### Sandbox and platform support

- Expanded managed sandbox metadata support on macOS and Linux, including narrower filesystem profiles, deny rules, protected metadata paths, and clearer fail-closed behavior. (#139, #144, #150, #156)
- Added Linux managed-domain allowlisting through the managed proxy while keeping direct worker egress blocked. (#161, #164)
- Added Windows network-policy parity for workspace-write sandboxes after one-time Windows sandbox setup. (#129)
- Clarified that `inherit-codex` requires Codex per-call sandbox metadata; other MCP clients should use explicit sandbox modes. (#167)

### Packaging and maintenance

- Switched releases to immutable tag-driven publishing with GitHub release archives and PyPI Trusted Publishing. (#142)
- Added a manual PyPI-only backfill path for existing release tags. (#151, #153)
- Updated installer behavior so REPL tools remain visible in code-mode configs with tool allowlists or blocklists. (#146, #157)
- Updated direct dependencies, made Rust warnings fail CI/release checks, and made restart, timeout, sandbox, and UTF-8 tests more deterministic. (#154, #158, #162, #163)

title: Clarify sandbox inheritance mode
description:

title: Protect managed-network sockets and preserve reset output
description:
## Summary
- Public-facing: On Linux, managed-network bridge sockets now live under a private session subdirectory that is mounted read-only in bubblewrap, so sandboxed workers can connect without being able to replace the socket path entries.
- Public-facing: Ctrl-D reset/restart now requests worker shutdown over sideband before worker-specific stdin handling, preserving already accepted R/Python input long enough to return old-worker shutdown output before any fresh-session tail output.
- Internal-only: The Linux bridge validates absolute socket paths in a shared directory, replaces stale relay-directory symlinks with a real directory, and cleans up relay socket files plus the private directory.
- Internal-only: Session-end and Zod timing tests now wait for observable startup markers or warm the session before timing-sensitive assertions; docs describe the new shutdown contract.

title: Deny rustc warnings and skip unavailable sandbox tests
description:
## Summary

This change makes rustc warnings fail local verification and CI, including release builds, so release-only dead code cannot merge quietly. It also lets restricted local test runs complete by skipping tests whose setup requires host capabilities that the active sandbox denies.

## User-facing changes

- No runtime behavior change for normal server use.
- Local contributors now see rustc warnings fail during documented verification and CI.
- `cargo test` can complete in restricted sandbox environments, with explicit skip banners for tests that require unavailable loopback sockets, host network access, or host sandbox execution.

## Internal changes

- Removed the unused restart wrapper and sideband restart-shutdown mode; debug restart now uses the same Ctrl-D restart path as the public tool flow.
- Set warning-denial Rust flags in CI and release workflows and added docs-contract coverage for that policy.
- Added dynamic test precondition checks for loopback sockets, host sandbox availability, and disabled outer network access.

title: Enable Linux managed domain allowlisting
description:
## Summary

This closes the Linux managed-domain allowlisting slice by enabling the existing allowlist policy on the bubblewrap sandbox path. The change keeps the public policy surface unchanged while making Linux fail closed when the active sandbox mode cannot enforce domain rules.

## User-facing changes

- `workspace-write` with `network_access=true` and `permissions.network.allowed_domains` now works on Linux when bubblewrap is enabled.
- Proxy-aware tools can reach allowlisted domains through the managed proxy while direct worker egress stays blocked.
- Linux managed-domain launches now return an actionable error when bubblewrap is disabled or legacy Landlock is selected.
- The sandbox docs now describe the Linux bubblewrap-only managed-domain behavior and remaining follow-up policy work.

## Internal changes

- Adds session-temp Unix relay sockets and namespace-local bridge listeners for HTTP and SOCKS traffic inside the bubblewrap network namespace.
- Adds an isolated proxy-routed Linux network mode that keeps `--unshare-net` and applies the proxy-routed seccomp profile only inside that namespace.
- Disables bubblewrap startup fallback when managed domains are configured.
- Adds Linux unit and public integration coverage for allowlisted proxy traffic, disallowed proxy traffic, and blocked direct sockets.

title: Add PyPI uvx alias
description:
## Summary

Adds a PyPI wheel-only `posit-mcp-repl` command so `uvx posit-mcp-repl` works directly, while keeping the project name and default Cargo-installed binary surface unchanged.

## User-facing changes

- Documents `uvx posit-mcp-repl --help` as the one-off PyPI invocation.
- PyPI wheels expose both `mcp-repl` and `posit-mcp-repl`; `cargo install` still exposes only `mcp-repl` by default.

## Internal changes

- Moves the shared CLI/server entrypoint into `src/lib.rs`, with small binary launchers for `mcp-repl` and the PyPI alias.
- Gates the alias binary behind a `pypi-alias` feature and configures maturin to enable it for wheel builds.
- Extends CI/release wheel smoke checks and contract tests to cover the alias command.

title: Stabilize restart handling and quiet CI test output
description:
## Summary

Extracts CI and test-stability fixes from the larger reset-tool cleanup work so they can merge independently. The main focus is making restart behavior deterministic under timed-out or background work, reducing successful test noise, and trimming incidental wait time in tests without changing the public MCP API.

## User-facing changes

- Clarifies reset behavior in user-facing docs: resets return already captured output, shut down the old worker in a bounded window, and run any remaining input in the fresh session.
- Preserves `repl_reset` and keeps it on the sideband shutdown path.
- Clarifies that explicit Ctrl-D restarts do not carry old shutdown-time output into later replies.
- Adds testing docs for focused quiet/fast local iteration.

## Internal changes

- Splits restart shutdown handling so `repl_reset` uses sideband shutdown while explicit Ctrl-D restart closes stdin and uses bounded termination.
- Snapshots restart output before shutdown so output produced while abandoning an old timed-out session does not leak into the restart reply or the next session.
- Preserves pager state across restart output handling.
- Increases the output-reader completion settle window to reduce timing-sensitive completion races.
- Captures spawned test-server stderr in the Rust harness with a bounded tail buffer, exposed through `McpTestSession::server_stderr_text()`, so expected negative-path diagnostics stay out of passing logs.
- Replaces several fixed sleeps in Python and zod tests with marker-file or log gates.
- Shortens non-contract restart snapshot timeouts from the default/long timeout path to explicit short timeouts.
- Silences non-contract R plot cleanup output by wrapping cleanup-only `grDevices::dev.off()` calls in `invisible(...)` and updates snapshots.

title: Update dependencies and harden R startup setup
description:
## Summary

Updates the dependency graph and R startup setup so fresh installs avoid stale dependency warnings while missing or unusual R installations fail with a controlled startup error.

## User-facing changes

- `cargo install --path .` no longer reports stale direct dependencies or the Linux Landlock deprecation warning.
- R startup now reports a structured `failed to start R session` / `failed to set up R_HOME` error when `R` or `R_HOME` cannot be resolved, instead of surfacing an early worker panic or raw worker exit.
- Fresh installs may still report `generic-array v0.14.7` as available for update because it is pinned by the upstream crypto dependency stack.

## Internal changes

- Bumped direct Rust dependencies, updated the Ark `harp`/`libr` revision, and refreshed `Cargo.lock`.
- Replaced `r_home_setup()` usage with local R home discovery that checks `R_HOME`, falls back to `R RHOME`, validates the path, and runs R commands against the resolved home.
- Updated Unix embedded R sandbox discovery to avoid treating an empty `R_HOME` as valid.
- Adjusted tests for newer `rmcp` APIs and made shared behavior test helpers run with `--sandbox danger-full-access` so they are not affected by the caller sandbox.

title: Remove the `repl_reset` tool
Fix Linux sandbox review regressions

title: Make timing tests deterministic across platforms
description:
## Summary

This tidies platform-specific timing behavior that had accumulated in tests and output finalization. The main issue was that some tests handled slow platforms by sleeping longer or gating coverage by OS, which made timing races harder to reason about.

This also addresses the macOS CI flake seen on PR 150: completion settling could finalize after split UTF-8 output recovery before the remaining output arrived.

## User-facing changes

No intentional CLI or protocol changes.

Request completion now uses the same output-stability wait across platforms, which should make completion output handling less timing-sensitive.

## Internal changes

- Removed the macOS-only completion-stability branch in request finalization.
- Made the zod split UTF-8 completion tests run on all platforms.
- Replaced platform-specific sleeps in timeout, sandbox metadata, file output, reticulate, and pager tests with observable state waits.
- Deleted a redundant racy timeout-bundle test.
- Simplified platform timeout helpers that no longer expressed platform-specific behavior.
- Added a completed plan note documenting the cleanup decisions.

## Notes

This PR does not try to consolidate the existing sandbox test matrix. Some current sandbox gates cover backend-specific launch paths, but several public allow/deny tests likely can be made more cross-platform in a follow-up cleanup.

title: Relax manual PyPI backfill checks
description:
## Summary

Relax manual PyPI backfill runs so they do not rerun validation checks from the current release workflow against historical tags. A backfilled tag is assumed to have satisfied the checks that were required when the tag was originally created; the manual path should only rebuild and smoke-test the artifacts needed to publish `posit-mcp-repl`.

## User-facing changes

- Clarifies the release guide for manual PyPI backfills.
- Documents that manual backfills build and smoke-test the release binary and PyPI wheels, then publish only to PyPI.
- Documents that manual backfills do not rerun historical validation checks.

## Internal changes

- Keeps full check, test, lint, formatting, client integration, release CLI contract, and GitHub Release archive steps on tag-push releases only.
- Leaves manual dispatches with tag/version validation, release build, binary smoke test, PyPI wheel build, wheel smoke test, wheel artifact upload, and PyPI publishing.
- Updates docs-contract coverage so the manual path cannot drift back toward rerunning the current validation matrix.

title: Make request output finalization explicit
description:
## Summary

Refactor request output finalization so completion, timeout, session-end/error/reset paths, marker insertion, and UTF-8 tail sealing use explicit server-side policies instead of marker side effects.

This keeps the worker sideband protocol unchanged while making the server's output timeline contract clearer: markers are ordering facts, and UTF-8 tails are sealed only by named presentation policies.

## Public-facing changes

- Preserve split UTF-8 output when continuation bytes arrive during completion settling, including after normal output-reader quiescence.
- Keep `timeout_ms` as a hard response budget: timeout replies do not wait for the UTF-8 tail recovery window after expiry.
- Continue exposing already-buffered visible output, such as images or stderr, behind an incomplete UTF-8 tail in timeout replies.
- Prevent stderr rendering state from leaking across request boundaries after an incomplete UTF-8 tail is later sealed.

## Internal changes

- Make `input_wait`, `request_boundary`, and `session_end` pure timeline markers that do not implicitly drain or seal UTF-8 state.
- Replace generic UTF-8 flushing calls with explicit seal policies for final drains and timeout-visible-output drains.
- Add deadline-aware request output outcomes for completed, timed-out, and failed completion waits.
- Add zod fixture commands and public regressions for completion, timeout, and request-boundary UTF-8 behavior.
- Make busy follow-up bundle tests deterministic with file gates instead of scheduler sleeps.
- Document the timeline marker and UTF-8 sealing contract, and record the completed design plan.

## Testing

title: Add manual PyPI backfill release path
description:
## Summary

Add a narrow manual PyPI backfill path to the existing release workflow so `posit-mcp-repl` can be published for an existing release tag when downstream plugin work is blocked before the next scheduled tag.

## User-facing changes

- Documents a `Release` workflow manual dispatch using `pypi_backfill_tag`.
- Makes the constraints explicit: existing immutable semver tags only, PyPI-only publishing, no dev release, no tag movement, no GitHub Release repair, and no sdist upload.

## Internal changes

- Reuses the release check matrix for tag pushes and manual dispatches.
- Keeps GitHub Release publishing limited to tag pushes.
- Lets manual dispatches overlay current `pyproject.toml` metadata for tags that predate PyPI packaging while compiling source from the immutable tag.
- Skips the release CLI contract only when an old tag lacks that test file.
- Updates docs-contract coverage for the new release workflow contract and release guide text.

title: Make Linux sandboxing bwrap-first for managed profiles
description:
## Summary

Rework Linux sandbox enforcement so managed filesystem profiles use bubblewrap by default, with legacy Landlock retained as an explicit fallback.

## Changes

- Accept managed filesystem profiles on Linux instead of rejecting them as macOS-only.
- Render restricted reads, :minimal, project-root entries, temp special paths, deny paths/globs, and protected .git/.codex/.agents paths into the Linux bubblewrap mount plan.
- Preserve symlinked and missing writable roots in the bwrap mount plan, and fail closed when legacy Landlock cannot represent managed writable-root carveouts.
- Keep client-provided sandbox helper paths ignored; mcp-repl continues to launch its own internal helper.
- Preserve seccomp-based network and process restrictions, while continuing to fail closed for unsupported managed domain allowlists on Linux.
- Route Linux bwrap interrupts to sandboxed worker descendants instead of the bwrap monitor.
- Preserve split UTF-8 tails across input-wait/request-boundary drains.
- Update sandbox docs and add an active follow-up plan for remaining Linux sandbox parity work.

## Validation

- `cargo check`
- `cargo build`
- `python3 tests/run_integration_tests.py --binary target/debug/mcp-repl`
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test --quiet`
- `cargo +nightly fmt`

## Follow-ups

- Bundle or probe bubblewrap more explicitly so behavior is less dependent on the host bwrap.
- Add Linux managed-network proxy routing for domain allowlists.
- Add full protected-create monitoring for missing metadata paths.

title: Improve CLI help and hide debug REPL in release builds
description:
## Summary

This improves the CLI help output and tightens the shipped release-binary contract around dev-only debug REPL support.

## Public-facing changes

- Reworks `mcp-repl --help` and `mcp-repl install --help` into wrapped, sectioned help text.
- Clarifies that `mcp-repl` is an MCP server meant to be launched by a configured client or harness.
- Removes `--debug-repl` from shipped release binaries and documents that it is only available in debug/dev builds.
- Notes that files-mode oversized output expects filesystem access for reading bundle files.

## Internal-only changes

- Gates debug REPL code paths behind `debug_assertions`.
- Adds CLI coverage for wrapped help output and install help output.
- Adds a release CLI contract test that verifies release binaries do not expose or accept `--debug-repl`.
- Runs that release contract in the release workflow for Unix and Windows release binaries.

title: Preserve split UTF-8 across input waits
description:
## Summary

- Preserve incomplete raw UTF-8 tails when a request completes at `input_wait`, so a continuation byte captured after the marker can still render as one character.
- Keep sealing behavior for session end and the next accepted request, preventing cross-request UTF-8 merges.
- Strengthen the zod protocol regression by delaying the continuation byte after `input_wait`.

## Public-facing changes

Files-mode output no longer escapes a split raw UTF-8 character when `input_wait` is observed before the output reader captures the continuation byte.

## Internal-only changes

- Added `drain_completed_formatted_output` to centralize completed-output drain semantics.
- Updated the zod worker fixture and regression timing.

## Testing

title: Respect console plot sizing during R drawing
description:
## Summary

R console plot sizing options now control the managed graphics device while plotting code is drawing, not only the replayed PNG export. This fixes device-aware layout code that reads `dev.size()`, `par("pin")`, or text metrics during plot construction.

## User-facing changes

- `options(console.plot.width, console.plot.height, console.plot.units, console.plot.dpi)` now affect the live managed R plot device.
- Added `console.plot.asp` as height / width, matching the shape of knitr `fig.asp` and Quarto `fig-asp`.
- Documented that explicit user-opened graphics devices remain user-controlled.

## Internal changes

- Shared plot-size resolution between managed device creation and replay/export.
- Track the managed device by backing filepath as well as device number, so stale device numbers do not cause explicit user devices to be resized.
- Added public MCP plot tests for live device geometry, aspect ratio, precedence, resizing on new managed pages, and explicit user devices.

title: Expose REPL tools in code mode installs
description:
## Summary
Make the OpenAI CLI install path expose the R and Python REPL MCP namespaces directly in code mode, so installed tools remain visible after setup.

title: Render managed sandbox metadata directly on macOS
description:
## Summary

This PR makes inherited managed sandbox metadata authoritative for macOS worker launches. Instead of flattening per-call metadata into the older read-only, workspace-write, external-sandbox, or full-access shapes, mcp-repl now renders the managed filesystem and network profile directly into Seatbelt while keeping existing CLI sandbox arguments available.

This lets current MCP clients preserve narrower filesystem and network semantics on macOS, including explicit readable and writable roots, special paths, deny rules, and restricted network state.

## User-Facing Changes

- `--sandbox inherit` on macOS supports managed permission profiles with readable roots, writable roots, special paths, deny roots/globs, and restricted network state.
- Minimal inherited profiles remain practical for R startup and Python workflows that use libomp-style shared-memory registration.
- Read-only and minimal profiles stay narrow: only explicitly granted temp roots are writable, while the server-owned session temp directory remains available for worker startup.
- Existing mcp-repl sandbox CLI arguments continue to work.

## Internal Changes

- Adds a managed filesystem policy model and projects legacy CLI modes into it for macOS Seatbelt rendering.
- Reworks macOS Seatbelt generation to emit read, write, deny, glob-deny, platform-default, and network policy sections from managed policy.
- Moves restricted read-only platform defaults into a dedicated Seatbelt include and adds targeted R/Python runtime carve-outs.
- Handles path aliases and nested allow/deny relationships when rendering sandbox roots.
- Keeps managed policy enforcement macOS-only for now; Linux and Windows reject managed policies at validation boundaries.
- Expands regression coverage for inherited metadata, deny behavior, minimal R startup, Python shared-memory registration, and temp-root behavior.
- Enables embedded R module assets in debug builds so startup does not depend on source checkout reads.

title: Rework Linux sandbox around permission profiles
description:
## Summary

The change is Linux-focused and keeps older local sandbox modes as adapters into the new policy shape.

## User-Facing Changes

- Existing CLI arguments remain supported, including `--sandbox`, `--add-writable-root`, `--add-allowed-domain`, and the current sandbox-related `--config` keys.
- `permissionProfile` is now the canonical inherited sandbox metadata shape; legacy `sandboxPolicy` metadata is still accepted as a minimal compatibility input and converted immediately.
- Linux workers now prefer bubblewrap when available, with legacy Landlock as a fallback when bubblewrap cannot start.
- `MCP_REPL_USE_LINUX_BWRAP=1` forces a bubblewrap attempt; `MCP_REPL_USE_LINUX_BWRAP=0` uses the legacy Landlock path.
- Restricted-read profiles are accepted. Exact read enforcement requires bubblewrap; the legacy Landlock fallback still enforces writable roots but broadens reads to host-readable paths.

## Internal Changes

- Adds `src/sandbox/codex_policy.rs` with `PermissionProfile`, filesystem policy, network policy, path resolution, and legacy policy conversion.
- Changes `SandboxState` to track both the compatibility `SandboxPolicy` and the effective permission profile.
- Updates Linux helper launch to consume `--permission-profile`, build bubblewrap mounts from the new policy model, and apply restricted-network seccomp in the final worker process.
- Keeps `codexLinuxSandboxExe` accepted as incoming metadata but does not expose it as worker runtime state.
- Extends worker context logging with `permission_profile` and `use_legacy_landlock`.
- Updates sandbox docs, the completed implementation plan, and focused sandbox metadata coverage.

title: Unify output timeline rendering
description:
## Summary

Unifies server-side output rendering around one `OutputTimeline` and a shared resolved-output projection layer. Normal replies, files-mode bundles, pager pages, images, server notices, stderr prefixes, and generated input echoes now flow through the same ordering model instead of separate files-mode and pager merge paths.

Generated input echoes are represented as timeline events from sideband input metadata. They are hidden from normal `repl` replies, retained as transcript-only context for output-bundle transcripts and pager transcript rendering, and never used to match, inspect, or suppress captured stdout/stderr.

The branch also tightens output retention and projection edge cases so hidden generated echoes do not consume visible pager budget, create output gaps, add stale stderr separators, or evict later visible text/images under bundle quota pressure.

## Public-facing changes

- Normal `repl` replies hide generated submitted-input/readline echoes.
- Output-bundle transcripts include generated echoes in `transcript.txt` so spilled output retains consumed-input context.
- Prompt-shaped stdout/stderr and worker `output_text` remain visible, even when they match submitted input.
- Pager pages are sized around visible output, not transcript-only generated echoes.
- Split UTF-8 output preserves ordering across stderr, images, timeout drains, and session-end notices.
- Files-mode bundle quota handling preserves later reply-visible text and images before hidden echo content.
- Stderr prefixes remain stable across pager continuations, partial output, resets, and hidden echo events.

## Internal changes

- Adds `src/resolved_output.rs` for shared projection from timeline ranges into `WorkerContent`.
- Adds `ContentVisibility::TranscriptOnly` and `OutputEventKind::InputEcho`.
- Replaces the files-mode pending-output formatter with a facade over the shared `OutputTimeline`.
- Removes the pager-specific merge path and routes pager/files replay through the shared renderer.
- Adds UTF-8 tail buffering in `OutputTimeline` so incomplete byte sequences do not reorder following events.
- Adds head-retention support for files-mode timelines so hidden echoes can be dropped before visible output.
- Updates output-bundle reservation and omission handling for transcript-only text and reply-visible images.
- Updates output timeline docs and marks the unified output timeline plan complete.

## Coverage

- Adds/regenerates unit, snapshot, and integration coverage for pager pages, files-mode bundles, Zod protocol workers, Python help/plot behavior, split UTF-8 ordering, stderr prefixing, output bundle quotas, and external integration expectations.

title: Add Python repl_prepare runtime preparation
description:
## Summary

Adds a Python-only `repl_prepare` tool for cases where a caller wants to change, select, or preflight the Python environment before later `repl` calls. The Python REPL itself still starts ready for evaluation; `repl_prepare` is for environment preparation, not for making `repl` usable.

## Tool schema

`repl_prepare` is advertised only by Python servers when `uv` is available. R servers continue to advertise `repl_reset`; Python servers no longer advertise `repl_reset`.

```ts
repl_prepare({
  requirements?: {
    packages?: string[];
    python_version?: string;
    action?: "add" | "remove" | "set";      // default: "add"
    restart?: "if_needed" | "no" | "yes";   // default: "if_needed"
  };
  python?: {
    executable?: string; // absolute path
    venv?: string;       // absolute path to a virtual environment
  };
})
```

Contract details:

- Do not call `repl_prepare` just to make `repl` available; the REPL starts ready.
- Use `requirements` when the caller needs managed packages or a managed Python version before evaluation.
- Use `python` when the caller needs an existing interpreter or virtual environment.
- Omit all arguments only to realize the current managed requirements manifest without changing it.
- The managed manifest starts as `packages=["numpy"]` and `python_version=null`.
- Provide either `requirements` or `python`, not both.
- Inside `python`, provide exactly one of `executable` or `venv`.
- `requirements.action` updates the persistent managed manifest with `add`, `remove`, or `set`.
- `requirements.restart` controls whether preparation may restart the active Python session.
- `requirements.python_version` is forwarded to `uv` as supplied.
- Explicit `python` selections use the requested interpreter or venv as-is and do not mutate the managed manifest.
- The tool does not execute user code, import packages, attach modules, or define aliases.
- There is no `timeout_ms` argument.

## Scenario examples

The snippets below use pseudo tool-call syntax. Each `repl(...)` call is a later Python REPL evaluation after `repl_prepare(...)` returns.

Add a package before importing it:

```python
repl_prepare(requirements = {packages: ["pandas"]})

repl("""
import pandas as pd
print(pd.DataFrame({"x": [1, 2]}).shape)
""")
# (2, 1)
```

Build up a persistent managed manifest:

```python
repl_prepare(requirements = {packages: ["pandas"]})
repl_prepare(requirements = {packages: ["plotnine"]})

repl("""
import pandas
import plotnine
print("ready")
""")
# ready
```

Replace the whole managed manifest and request a Python version constraint:

```python
repl_prepare(requirements = {
  packages: ["numpy", "pandas"],
  python_version: ">=3.11,<3.13",
  action: "set"
})

repl("""
import sys
import numpy
import pandas
print(sys.version_info >= (3, 11))
""")
# True
```

Preserve existing session state if preparation would require a restart:

```python
repl("_marker = 'kept'")

repl_prepare(requirements = {
  packages: ["plotnine"],
  restart: "no"
})
# returns an error if satisfying the request requires a restart
# session unchanged; no user state discarded

repl("print(_marker)")
# kept
```

Force a fresh session for the current managed manifest:

```python
repl("_marker = 'discarded'")

repl_prepare(requirements = {restart: "yes"})
# session restarted; user state discarded

repl("print('_marker' in globals())")
# False
```

Switch to an existing project virtual environment:

```python
repl_prepare(python = {venv: "/absolute/path/to/project/.venv"})

repl("""
import sys
print(sys.prefix)
""")
# /absolute/path/to/project/.venv
```

Switch to an explicit Python executable:

```python
repl_prepare(python = {executable: "/absolute/path/to/python"})

repl("""
import sys
print(sys.executable)
""")
# /absolute/path/to/python
```

Remove a package from the managed manifest before returning to that managed environment:

```python
repl_prepare(requirements = {packages: ["plotnine"], action: "remove"})

repl("""
import importlib.util
print(importlib.util.find_spec("plotnine") is None)
""")
# True
```

Reset Python without environment preparation:

```python
repl("<Ctrl-D>")
# new session started
```

R keeps the existing reset tool:

```r
repl_reset()
# new session started
```

## Internal changes

- Adds Python runtime preparation and requirement resolution through `uv`.
- Propagates prepared Python executable and module search-path overrides into embedded Python workers.
- Adds worker replacement support and lightweight user-state tracking for restart decisions.
- Splits server tool surfaces into R reset, Python prepare, and Python repl-only variants.
- Adds public MCP coverage for tool listing, schema validation, manifest updates, restart policy behavior, active-work replacement, and explicit Python selection.

## Diff composition

Measured against the merge base with `main`, this PR is `2079` insertions and `107` deletions across `22` files.

- runtime `src/`: `+1058/-95` (`52.7%` of churn)
- inline tests inside `src/`: `+3/-0` (`0.1%` of churn)

title: Unify worker turn input over IPC
description:
## Summary

This standardizes worker communication around an opaque IPC turn protocol so the server can treat R, Python, and protocol workers the same way. Managed input now flows through `turn_start` and `turn_input`; workers own how that input reaches their runtime and report completion with `idle` or `stdin_wait`.

The change removes the old dual-path stdin/PTY feed accounting that made completion and interrupt behavior harder to reason about. Reset and teardown now use an explicit `shutdown` lifecycle message before falling back to stdin close and bounded process termination.

## User-facing changes

- Stdin-style waits use a consistent continuation path across R and Python.
- Python help and stdin prompts are surfaced more consistently in transcript output.
- Reset and worker teardown are more reliable because shutdown no longer depends on stdin EOF.

- Replaced private stdin/PTY feed messages with shared `turn_start`, `turn_input`, `interrupt`, and `shutdown` IPC messages.
- Removed the built-in adapter request-state layer.
- Moved R and Python managed input behind worker-owned queues.
- Preserved active turn state across `stdin_wait` so follow-up input routes as `turn_input`.
- Updated protocol, architecture, debugging, testing, ADR, plan, and future-work docs.

title: Make worker interrupts cleanup-only and runtime-native
description:
This PR redraws worker interrupt handling so sideband IPC only performs ordered cleanup of unconsumed managed input, while actual runtime interruption always comes from the platform signal/control-event path.

The goal is to keep the server backend-neutral: non-empty client input is still sent as opaque `input_batch`, the worker owns where that input is consumed, and sideband cleanup never injects Python, R, or backend-specific interrupt state.

## Public-facing changes

- Bump the worker sideband protocol from v6 to v7.
- Replace sideband `interrupt` with `discard_pending_input { discard_id }`.
- Add `discard_pending_input_ack { discard_id, discarded_input }`.
- Remove worker-to-server `ready`; prompt-free readiness is now `input_wait { prompt: null }`.
- Allow `input_wait.prompt` and `input_line.prompt` to be `null` for prompt-free readiness and hidden input echo.
- Define Ctrl-C as: ordered sideband cleanup, real platform interrupt delivery, then optional tail dispatch after a short settle window.
- Keep platform interrupts mandatory even when cleanup ack times out or encounters a protocol error.
- On Windows PTY/ConPTY workers, deliver Ctrl-C through terminal input / `CTRL_C_EVENT`; pipe-only Windows workers do not claim targeted Ctrl-C support.

## Internal changes

- Centralize interrupt sequencing in the server/worker supervisor instead of backend-specific driver hooks.
- Correlate discard acknowledgements and reject unsolicited or mismatched acks as protocol errors.
- Split Python and R managed-input cleanup from runtime interrupt state.
- Remove Python IPC-side interrupt injection; Python now observes real signals through signal-aware waits.
- Make R input waits observe platform interrupt state through runtime wake plumbing.
- Update Windows ConPTY launch, shutdown, stdio wrapping, Ctrl-C delivery, and terminal-noise filtering for built-in and custom workers.
- Extend zod, Python, R, interrupt, sandbox, and docs-contract tests around ack ordering, ack timeout, stale/preemptive ack rejection, prompt-null readiness, Ctrl-C tail dispatch, and Windows signal behavior.
- Add a completed design record for the interrupt sideband boundary.

Windows was not failing because the Rust suite needed to be fully serial. title: Make built-in Python input demand-driven
description:
## Summary

Move built-in Python input toward the worker-owned v3 turn model. The server sends Python execution text over sideband `turn_start`, and the worker requests PTY/ConPTY input one unit at a time through private built-in messages. This keeps Python on true TTY stdio while request-boundary accounting stays with the worker instead of depending on eager server stdin writes.

## User-facing changes

- Python nested input states such as `help()` now return an explicit `<<repl status: waiting for stdin>>` status while preserving prompt text in the transcript.
- Python reset/interrupt handling is tightened so queued tail input is not consumed after a blocked input prompt.
- Ctrl-C-prefixed follow-up input is covered so the next turn's readline input is preserved.

## Internal changes

- Adds private built-in sideband messages for PTY feeding, stdin wait status, and follow-up turn input.
- Keeps built-in Python on protocol v3 after merging the Windows ConPTY support from `main`.
- Removes legacy protocol v2/backend-info handling and renames remaining built-in adapter bookkeeping away from legacy protocol terminology.
- Documents the boundary between public custom-worker v3 semantics and temporary built-in adapter bridge messages.
- Updates Python backend tests, docs-contract coverage, and help snapshots for the demand-driven waiting behavior.

title: Add Windows Python ConPTY turn support
description:
## Summary

This rebuilds Windows Python PTY support against the current worker-owned turn protocol. The motivation is to make Windows Python behave like a real interactive terminal without reviving the retired server-visible stdin accounting model: accepted input enters the worker via `turn_start`, and only the worker can complete a turn with `idle(turn_id)` once it reaches a safe input boundary.

## User-Facing Changes

- Windows Python sessions now expose TTY-backed fd `0/1/2` at both Python `os.isatty()` and native CRT `_isatty()` layers.
- CPython uses its normal interactive `PyRun_InteractiveOneFlags` / `PyOS_ReadlineFunctionPointer` path on Windows instead of a Windows-only `runsource` loop.
- `input()`, `sys.stdin`, `os.read(0, ...)`, duplicated stdin fds, fd replacement, CRLF input, Unicode input, and buffered answers work on the Windows PTY path.

title: Preserve raw worker stdin at the server boundary

## Summary

It also updates control-prefixed input handling so `Ctrl-C`/`Ctrl-D` consume only the control byte. Any immediate newline remains part of the follow-up input, so `Ctrl-D` is a bare restart, while `Ctrl-D\n` is a restart followed by a blank input and `Ctrl-D\nfoo` is a restart followed by the leading blank line plus `foo`.

Protocol-worker shutdown handling is hardened by validating `session_end.reason` and optional `message_b64`, and reset handling now snapshots output before graceful shutdown so teardown-only output does not leak into the `new session started` reply.

## Public Facing Changes

- `repl` stdin preserves supplied CRLF and bare-CR bytes at the server boundary, with only the final-newline append rule.
- `Ctrl-C`/`Ctrl-D` followed by newline is treated as a control action with follow-up input, not as a bare control.
- Invalid protocol-worker `session_end` metadata now fails as a protocol error instead of being accepted as a clean shutdown.

## Internal Changes

- Expanded the Zod fixture with deterministic hooks for raw stdin reporting, interrupt facts, buffered-stdin discard, active stdin reads, delayed/hanging shutdown, and malformed `session_end` frames.
- Added Zod protocol coverage for stdin preservation, control-tail newlines, interrupt delivery, reset EOF behavior, shutdown hooks, and protocol validation.

title: Move R stdin handling onto the worker protocol timeline
description:
## Motivation

This is an architecture cleanup for the worker/server boundary.

Historically, worker structural facts traveled over sideband while much of the visible output traveled over stdout/stderr. That forced the server to reconstruct a single timeline from separate channels, which led to timing-sensitive behavior, prompt/output reconciliation, and backend-specific gating.

The target shape is simpler: worker-owned output and stdin facts arrive pre-ordered on the protocol timeline. Raw stdout/stderr remain as fallback for unowned output, mostly from forked child processes where deterministic ordering is not guaranteed anyway.

This PR moves R further into that model by making R request handling stdin-accounted and protocol-driven instead of relying on transitional request metadata.

## Summary

- Move the built-in R worker off transitional `stdin_write` request handling.
- Use `begin_request_with_stdin()` so the server accounts for R input generically.
- Have the R worker read stdin directly and enqueue input into the R session.
- Emit `readline_input` for R input delivered to the runtime-facing console layer.
- Emit `readline_discard` for queued R input discarded during interrupt cleanup.
- Add MCP-level coverage for a custom-launched R worker using the generic protocol path.
- Update protocol docs to state that built-in R no longer uses transitional stdin frames.

## Public-facing changes

Existing R MCP behavior should be preserved. This is primarily an internal boundary change.

## Internal changes

- Removes R-specific request channel and active-request completion bookkeeping.
- Reduces server knowledge of R request state.
- Keeps transitional stdin frames available for Python compatibility, but R no longer consumes them.
- Moves R closer to the language-agnostic worker contract where the worker owns runtime semantics and the server finalizes replies from ordered protocol facts.

title: Move Python stdin accounting to CPython readline via PTY
description:
## Summary

Move the supported Unix Python worker to PTY-backed C stdio so CPython treats stdin/stdout/stderr as terminal streams and consults `PyOS_ReadlineFunctionPointer` for interactive reads.

The intent is to make CPython readline the integration point for Python interactive input, `input()`, and debugger-style command loops while keeping sideband IPC separate from visible PTY traffic.

## Motivation

CPython only consults `PyOS_ReadlineFunctionPointer` when C stdin is TTY-backed. With ordinary pipes, that hook is not used, which forces a much wider worker-side interception surface: `builtins.input`, `sys.stdin`, `open(0)`, `os.read`, raw fd paths, and related REPL/input behavior.

That path is heavier and pushes the integration toward reimplementing interpreter surfaces. A PTY has its own complexity, especially for Windows, but for the supported Unix path it keeps the interpreter integration thinner: one primary integration point, fewer Python-level replacements, and more of Python's REPL behavior left to CPython.

## Public-Facing Changes

No intentional public-facing behavior change. This is an internal integration change intended to preserve the existing Python REPL surface while moving supported Unix stdin accounting onto CPython's native readline path.

PTY-backed stdio may still expose normal terminal semantics in edge cases, including CRLF translation, stdout/stderr stream merging, terminal width effects, echo handling, and `isatty()`-dependent behavior.

## Internal Changes

- Add a launch-time pipe-vs-PTY worker stdin transport abstraction.
- Run built-in Unix Python workers with PTY-backed C stdin/stdout/stderr while keeping sideband IPC on separate descriptors.
- Use the CPython readline callback as the stdin accounting point for interactive Python input.
- Harden interrupt and reset cleanup around PTY-backed readline state.
- Update Python backend coverage, plot-image coverage, protocol fixture coverage, and docs for the PTY output contract.

## Diff Size Note

This PR looks like a large addition because it carries transitional pipe-backed and non-Unix compatibility scaffolding while adding the supported Unix PTY path. A follow-up cleanup is logged and blocked on Windows ConPTY support; after that lands, most of the previous broad stdin interception and protocol compatibility code is slated for deletion.

title: Update Linux sandbox for latest codex compatibility
description:
## Summary

This PR updates `mcp-repl`'s Linux sandbox integration to stay compatible with latest release Codex behavior (`0.120.0`).

Concretely, it:

* refreshes the Linux Codex approval snapshots against the current local `codex` cli 0.120.0 output
* if installed with `mcp-repl --sandbox inherit`, changes behavior on Linux so that `mcp-repl` always launches Linux workers through `mcp-repl`'s internal sandbox helper, instead of honoring inherited `codexLinuxSandboxExe`
* continues to honor inherited sandbox policy and cwd, and maps newer inherited `useLegacyLandlock` updates onto `mcp-repl`'s internal `use_linux_sandbox_bwrap` setting
* retries Linux worker startup once without `bwrap` if the `bwrap` path dies before backend info arrives, and surfaces a fallback notice
* trims late echo-only suffixes from worker output and hardens the Codex approval/sandbox tests around newer transcript noise and environment-specific startup failures

## Why

`mcp-repl` should be able to inherit Codex's sandbox policy, but it should not use Codex's Linux helper executable. This is primarily because `mcp-repl` needs to modify the sandbox config to include configured carve-outs for the REPL, including things like user-configured additional writable roots (for example, a Quarto cache) and similar future sandbox exclusions we will want to support (for example, network allowlists), while still staying compatible with the sandbox state that newer Codex sessions send.

title: Refactor Windows sandbox setup to speed up and stabilize Windows tests
description:
## Summary

This refactors the Windows sandbox path so stable filesystem permission setup is prepared once by the parent process and reused across worker launches, without adding new persistent workspace metadata.

The main goal is to make the Windows test suite less flaky and much faster to run. In practice, that means less ACL work on restart, better handling of moved or newly created artifacts, more reliable Windows interrupt and wrapper teardown behavior, and much broader Windows regression coverage.

## Motivation

Before this change, Windows sandboxed REPL launches repeated filesystem and ACL setup work in the worker launch path on each session start, which made restart-heavy Windows tests slow. This moves that setup to the parent/server side so it can be prepared once per MCP session and reused across worker restarts.

The follow-up commits mostly tighten correctness around that split rather than broaden scope: recursive repair of nested workspace descendants, deny refresh for protected descendants, safer ACL rollback and teardown, stricter isolation for `MCP_REPL_R_SESSION_TMPDIR`, more reliable Windows interrupt delivery, and better bounded stdio shutdown.

## User-facing fixes

- fix a few small bugs and inconsistencies in how base R plots are surfaced on Windows
- clean up Ctrl-D restart notice presentation in files mode so the restart notice stays on its own line before follow-up output
- preserve idle restart notices during empty pager polls, and keep empty pager input polling for pending output before pager navigation
- improve Windows Ctrl-C handling so interrupt prefixes can interrupt the running request while still executing remaining input
- make busy follow-up behavior more reliable by keeping dropped-input handling explicit and preserving hidden timeout bundles as later output arrives

## Internal changes

- move most Windows filesystem permission setup out of the wrapper launch hot path into parent-owned prepared launch state
- cache and reuse that prepared state across worker restarts instead of recomputing permissions on every launch
- keep the prepared state in memory and derive stable workspace identity from the effective sandbox policy, rather than writing new per-workspace metadata files
- separate long-lived workspace permissions from per-launch permissions, so shared workspace access and per-session temp access are managed independently
- keep `MCP_REPL_R_SESSION_TMPDIR` launch-scoped instead of sharing it through the stable workspace SID, and avoid mistaking unrelated writable roots under `%TEMP%` for session temp trees just because they share the same filename prefix
- refresh prepared ACL state when files or directories are moved, renamed, created late, or need repair after a restart
- if an ACL update fails partway through, restore the previous permissions instead of leaving partially updated state behind; also make cleanup on restart and session exit more reliable for protected and nested paths
- fail fast on Windows sandbox prepare/startup errors that used to blur into test skips, including named-pipe startup failures
- keep the worker stdin gate Windows-only, remove the dead worker interrupt hook, deliver Windows R interrupts via `CTRL_BREAK_EVENT`, and switch embedded Windows R to `UImode_RTerm`
- make wrapper stdio shutdown bounded and progress-aware so it is less likely to hang or drop trailing output, and add traced stdio helper scripts for Windows debugging
- add a checkout-scoped Windows suite-server lock so test startup is serialized where needed without blocking separate live sessions

## Notes

- this also adds future-work notes for broader stdin ownership cleanup and a few remaining REPL interaction rough edges
- most of the implementation change is in `src/windows_sandbox.rs`, with most of the regression coverage added in `tests/sandbox.rs`

Add GitHub-hosted binary distribution for `mcp-repl` through GitHub Releases with two channels: a rolling `dev` prerelease that tracks the newest successful `main` build, and semver tag releases where final tags publish stable releases and prerelease tags publish GitHub prereleases.

This keeps downloadable binaries on GitHub Releases instead of temporary Actions artifacts while reusing the existing CI workflow for validation and publishing.

title: Spill oversized REPL replies to files via output bundles
description:
## Summary

This PR adds server-owned output bundles for oversized REPL replies and makes oversized-output handling an explicit runtime mode.

Bare `mcp-repl` still defaults to `pager`, but `mcp-repl install` now pins `--oversized-output files` for Codex and Claude unless the user already chose a mode. That keeps installed clients on the bundle-backed path while preserving pager mode as an explicit runtime option.

## Public-facing changes

- add `--oversized-output <files|pager>`
- keep bare `mcp-repl` on `pager` by default
- make `mcp-repl install` write `--oversized-output files` for Codex and Claude by default
- in `files` mode, keep oversized replies compact inline while disclosing bundle artifacts such as `transcript.txt`, `events.log`, `images/`, and `images/history/`
- update the R and Python tool descriptions to document the bundle-backed contract, and add pager-specific tool descriptions for explicit pager mode
- document that `repl_reset` does not immediately remove previously disclosed bundle artifacts, though old bundle paths may later disappear due to pruning or server exit

## Internal changes

- add a server-side pending-output tape and response finalizer to unify timeout handling, follow-up polls, detached output, and session-end finalization
- distinguish worker-originated text from server-originated notices so transcript files and mixed text/image bundles preserve the intended contract
- harden the worker IPC contract so startup IPC state is bootstrap-only and child processes cannot inherit or reuse sideband channels
- expand coverage for oversized text/image replies, timeout bundle reuse, bundle pruning, prompt/echo trimming, and related request-boundary edge cases

## Implementation path

This branch started by stripping back the default pager path to create a cleaner separation between modal pager behavior and file-backed oversized-output handling. That exposed how much timeout handling, request boundaries, prompt/echo cleanup, and detached output were still coupled to pager-era assumptions. The design then shifted toward a server-owned model: first capture pending output in one place, then finalize replies and bundle materialization at the server boundary.

A large part of the branch after that is the work needed to make that model hold under real REPL behavior rather than only on the happy path. The follow-on fixes are mostly about tightening boundaries once the architecture was clear: keeping worker text separate from server notices, making timeout bundle reuse deterministic, preserving image history without flooding inline replies, and preventing child processes from inheriting sideband IPC state. That path gives more confidence in the final implementation because the branch did not just add bundle output as a feature layer; it forced the request lifecycle, output ownership, and public contract to line up around the same server-side model.

## Miscellaneous / Errata

- add an agent-facing docs map plus new architecture and testing entrypoint docs
- simplify and tighten agent/planning guidance in `AGENTS.md` and `docs/plans/*`
- add docs contract tests to keep the docs layout and snapshot expectations in sync
- serialize the Windows CI test job to reduce platform-specific flakiness
- upgrade Rust dependencies, pin the `ark` revision, and bump the crate version to `0.2.0-dev`

title: Add Claude hook integration for session-scoped /clear resets
description:
## Summary

title: Add Claude hook integration for session-scoped /clear resets
description:
## Summary

This adds Claude hook integration so Claude `/clear` resets the correct `mcp-repl` session.

Claude does not expose the same direct session lifecycle plumbing that Codex uses, so `mcp-repl` has to coordinate Claude session resets through `SessionStart` / `SessionEnd` hooks plus `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE`. This branch adds that Claude-specific integration and puts guardrails around it so `/clear` resets the correct session when multiple Claude clients are active in the same checkout or when Claude starts subagents on a shared MCP connection.

Codex does not need this hook/env-file path because it already has its own session and sandbox update flow.

## Public-facing changes

- add `mcp-repl claude-hook <session-start|session-end>`
- make `install --client claude` update Claude MCP config, permissions, and top-level `SessionStart` / `SessionEnd` hooks in `settings.json`
- make Claude `/clear` reset the REPL worker bound to the hook's exact `(CLAUDE_ENV_FILE, MCP_REPL_CLAUDE_SESSION_ID)` pair
- support multiple Claude sessions in the same working directory without cross-resetting each other's REPL state
- preserve late binding when the server starts before Claude has written session metadata

## Internal changes

- add `src/claude.rs` to handle Claude hook parsing, session binding, instance records, and control-file restart requests
- bind Claude-owned workers to the exact `(CLAUDE_ENV_FILE, MCP_REPL_CLAUDE_SESSION_ID)` identity captured for that server process
- integrate Claude hook installation and updates into `install --client claude`, including top-level `SessionStart` / `SessionEnd` settings entries and command replacement/quoting
- support late binding when Claude session metadata appears after server startup, while preserving the existing inherited-sandbox startup ordering
- add regression and live integration coverage for hook installation, startup binding, late binding, exact-session clears, and concurrent same-directory Claude sessions

It also fixes compact-card correctness issues around same-line navigation, seen-range-aware paging guidance, and mixed stdout/stderr attribution.

## What Changed

- preserved search navigation state across `:matches`, `:goto`, refreshes, and cursor drift
- fixed compact search cards for long lines, UTF-8/invalid UTF-8 boundaries, and same-line backward/forward hits
- made forward search fall back to earlier hits after misses, with `:where` reporting the same behavior
- made `:where` suggest `:skip` based on unseen pages instead of raw buffer pages
- preserved stdout/stderr attribution in compact search cards, including mixed-stream snippets on the same physical line

description:
## Summary
This PR adds structured per-startup debug event logging and hardens startup/runtime paths that previously assumed UTF-8-only argv/env data. It also fixes sandbox inherit precedence and expands integration/regression coverage around Codex sandbox transitions and install behavior.

## Public-facing changes
- Added optional startup debug event logging:
  - CLI: `--debug-events-dir /path/to/log-dir`

- Fixed `--sandbox-state inherit` precedence so it clears inherited sandbox env state for process startup, while no sandbox flags now preserve existing env state.
- Kept Codex/Claude install behavior aligned and improved emitted config readability (notably paired JSON args formatting).

## Internal-only changes
- Added `src/event_log.rs` JSONL logger with startup context capture, sensitive `CODEX_*` env filtering, and lazy payload logging.
- Instrumented server/worker lifecycle and tool execution paths with structured events:
  - tool call begin/end/error
  - custom request/notification handling
  - sandbox update apply/fail
  - worker spawn/reset/restart/interrupt/shutdown
  - server run/listen/warm-start lifecycle
- Switched key argv/env reads to OS-string flows (`args_os` / `vars_os`-compatible) to avoid panics on non-UTF-8 input.

- Refactors install config generation to build per-client args and per-interpreter server entries.

- Implement Windows sandbox runner/token flow and ACL-based allow/deny path handling for `workspace-write` and `read-only` policies.

  - deterministic startup script parsing,

  - interrupt handling during active requests.
- Improve install-time home directory resolution for Windows env combinations.
- Mark Windows support as experimental and document current sandbox limitations.

### Test and docs updates

- Add and update regression tests for Windows IPC timeout/connect behavior, sandbox env/path handling, encoding behavior, and session lifecycle.
- Add Python interpreter selection tests and guard unsupported test paths by platform.
